tasks.subject: B5.3: Resumable checkpoints (immutable payload, ScoutmbError, completed_results)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A `CheckpointStore` port + `AtomicFileCheckpointStore` adapter persist which scouts (keyed by QR URL) are already complete and the attendee-to-output-UUID map, so a resumed run skips completed scouts and reuses their UUIDs -- landing `ACQ-RESUME-001/002/003/004`. The checkpoint payload is genuinely immutable (not merely typed `Mapping`), `CorruptCheckpoint` subclasses `ScoutmbError`, and `load()` rejects every malformed shape a hand-edited or corrupted file could take, not just a wrong version number.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/scoutmb/ports/checkpoint_store.py`, `src/scoutmb/adapters/files/checkpoint.py`
- Modify: `src/scoutmb/core/output_schemas.py` (add `scout_result_from_row`, the reverse of the existing `scout_result_to_row`, so a checkpoint's `completed_results` can be rehydrated into real `ScoutResult`s on resume -- Task B5.5 needs this to stop silently dropping previously-completed scouts from a resumed run's report)
- Test: `tests/unit/acquisition/test_checkpointing.py`, `tests/unit/test_output_schemas.py`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A run with no prior checkpoint file creates one on first save
- [ ] A scout whose QR URL is in `completed_urls` is skipped by the resume check
- [ ] The attendee-id-to-output-id map round-trips through save/load unchanged, and the loaded `Checkpoint.output_ids` cannot be mutated by mutating a dict the caller still holds a reference to
- [ ] `Checkpoint.completed_results` (one `scout_result_to_row`-shaped mapping per completed scout's URL) round-trips through save/load unchanged, and `scout_result_from_row` rebuilds an equal `ScoutResult` from any row `scout_result_to_row` produces (round-trip identity)
- [ ] `Checkpoint.completed_results` is immutable at BOTH levels -- the outer mapping AND each individual row dict -- mutating a row dict the caller still holds a reference to must not affect the constructed Checkpoint, and both the outer mapping and each row must raise TypeError on key assignment
- [ ] A checkpoint file with an unreadable/wrong-shaped body -- including a `completed_urls` that is a string, an `output_ids` that is a list, a `completed_results` that is a list or has non-string keys or non-object values, a `completed_results` entry whose URL is absent from `completed_urls` (an orphaned entry -- run_batch reconstructs results from completed_results.values() without cross-checking completed_urls, so an orphan would inject a bogus scout into the report), non-string keys or values inside `output_ids`, `version: true` (the bool-as-int hazard `core/output_schemas.py`'s own `check_schema_version` already documents), or invalid UTF-8 -- raises `CorruptCheckpoint` from `load()` rather than being partially trusted
- [ ] A checkpoint file saved before `completed_results` existed (no such key at all) still loads -- the field defaults to `{}` rather than treating the missing key as corruption, so old checkpoints from before this task remain readable
- [ ] `CorruptCheckpoint` subclasses `ScoutmbError`
- [ ] The save path is atomic (reuses `atomic_write_text`'s same-dir-temp-then-replace contract); a save that fails mid-replace leaves the prior checkpoint's bytes intact

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/unit/acquisition/test_checkpointing.py -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX (third pass): the second review round found 3 further checkpoint-semantics defects beyond this task's first-pass fixes -- checkpoints were marking failed scouts as completed, no checkpoint file existed until the first scout finished, and a resumed run's report silently dropped previously-completed scouts. This task's fix is `Checkpoint.completed_results` (MappingProxyType-wrapped, backward-compatible via `.get(..., {})` on load) plus `core/output_schemas.scout_result_from_row` (the reverse of `scout_result_to_row`), so a resumed run can reconstruct previously-completed scouts instead of dropping them. The actual completion-marking and fresh-checkpoint-at-start behavior live in Task B5.5's `run_batch()`, which is what composes this store into a real loop.

POST-CODEX FIX (fourth pass): an independent review found `completed_results` was only SHALLOWLY frozen -- the outer mapping was wrapped in MappingProxyType, but each row dict inside it stayed a plain mutable dict, contradicting the class's own "genuine read-only view" docstring claim. Fixed by wrapping each row in its own MappingProxyType too. The SAME review found `load()`'s validation for `completed_results` only checked "dict of str-to-dict" shape, weaker than every other field in this task -- a `completed_results` entry for a URL not present in `completed_urls` (a hand-edited or corrupted mismatch) would pass silently and later inject a bogus reconstructed scout into a resumed run's report. Fixed by requiring every `completed_results` key to be a subset of `completed_urls`.

```json:metadata
{"files": ["src/scoutmb/ports/checkpoint_store.py", "src/scoutmb/adapters/files/checkpoint.py", "src/scoutmb/core/output_schemas.py"], "verifyCommand": "uv run pytest tests/unit/acquisition/test_checkpointing.py tests/unit/test_output_schemas.py -q", "acceptanceCriteria": ["CorruptCheckpoint subclasses ScoutmbError", "output_ids and completed_results are genuinely immutable MappingProxyType views at every level, including nested rows", "load() strictly validates every field's shape including completed_results and its subset-of-completed_urls consistency", "completed_results round-trips via scout_result_from_row/scout_result_to_row", "backward compatible with checkpoints missing the completed_results key", "atomic save with preserved-bytes-on-failure test"], "modelTier": "standard"}
```

tasks.subject: B5.5: run_batch composes shared RetryPolicy + fail-closed checkpoint + RunIdentity hydration
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `run_batch()` composes one `RetryPolicy` (shared across every scout, so the breaker's cross-scout premise is actually satisfied), the `CheckpointStore` (skip completed scouts on resume, persist the attendee-to-output-UUID map after every scout), and `RunIdentity` hydration/snapshot into a single function that drives a whole run's scouts through `AcquisitionService`. This is the function `scout_schedule_cli.async_main` (sub-plan 4's Task B10.2) and `interfaces/cli/schedule.py` (sub-plan 3's `troop349-schedule`) both call.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/scoutmb/features/acquisition/batch.py`
- Modify: `src/scoutmb/core/identity.py` (add snapshot()/hydrate())
- Test: `tests/integration/test_acquisition_batch.py`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Single RetryPolicy shared across every scout; breaker opens based on cross-scout consecutive failures, proven with a real 3-scout test where the 3rd is never attempted
- [ ] run_batch checks check_closed() before each scout, records failure/success ONCE per scout (not per retry attempt)
- [ ] A scout in checkpoint.completed_urls is skipped entirely (service.process never called)
- [ ] run_batch() saves a fresh, empty Checkpoint immediately when there is no prior checkpoint file -- BEFORE the first scout is processed, not after -- landing ACQ-RESUME-001's "creates a fresh on-disk checkpoint file at the start of a run" behavior exactly
- [ ] A scout is added to completed_urls/completed_results ONLY when its ScoutResult.errors is empty -- a scout that raised or returned errors is NOT marked completed, so the next resume retries it rather than permanently skipping it
- [ ] After each scout, the checkpoint is saved with run_identity.snapshot() as output_ids -- a resumed run reuses the same output UUIDs even for a scout that failed this run
- [ ] A resumed run's returned list[ScoutResult] includes BOTH scouts reconstructed from the checkpoint's completed_results (via scout_result_from_row) AND scouts newly processed this run -- proven by a real two-sequential-run_batch-calls test
- [ ] A URL is skipped ONLY when it is in BOTH completed_urls AND completed_results -- a checkpoint saved before completed_results existed (Task B5.3's backward-compat load) has a URL in completed_urls with nothing in completed_results to reconstruct; that scout must be RE-PROCESSED, not silently dropped
- [ ] A FRESH RunIdentity hydrated from a saved checkpoint returns the same output_id for a known attendee (simulates process restart, not same-instance reuse)
- [ ] Between scouts (never after the last one actually processed), run_batch() sleeps via retry_policy.sleeper.sleep(...) for scout_delay_ms/1000 seconds when scout_delay_ms is given, else a random.uniform(0.5, 2.0) second delay -- matching legacy async_main's inter-scout pacing, which an earlier draft dropped entirely
- [ ] run_batch() prints the same two lines per scout legacy async_main did -- `[{index}/{total}] {label}` before processing and the `    attendeeID=..., classes=..., requirements=..., errors=...` summary after

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_acquisition_batch.py tests/unit/test_identity.py -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX (third pass): the second review round found this task's original draft unconditionally marked every attempted scout completed (including failed ones), never created a checkpoint file until the first scout happened to finish (contradicting ACQ-RESUME-001), silently dropped previously-completed scouts from a resumed run's report, and dropped scout_delay_ms/console progress output entirely when the inline async_main loop was extracted. All fixed: completion-marking now gated on `not result.errors`; an initial empty Checkpoint is saved at run_batch start before any scout runs (proven with a duck-typed `_ObservingService` that checks the checkpoint file's existence the moment `process()` is called); completed_results (Task B5.3) is read back via `scout_result_from_row` into the returned list; the exact legacy delay logic and print statements are restored.

POST-CODEX FIX (fourth pass): an independent review found the skip condition (`if scout.url in completed_urls:`) still silently drops a scout's result when resuming from a checkpoint saved before `completed_results` existed -- the exact bug `completed_results` was added to prevent, just triggered by an old-format file instead of a same-format one. Fixed by requiring the URL be present in BOTH `completed_urls` AND `completed_results` before skipping; for a same-version checkpoint the two sets are always in lockstep so this changes nothing, and for the backward-compat edge case it re-processes the scout once instead of losing it. See plan doc Task B5.5 in full.
